idea-plugin.name: Error Prone
idea-plugin.description:
Error Prone's findings in the editor, on the code they are about.

Error Prone already runs in your Gradle build. Its findings end up in the build log, as text with a file name and a line number, while the code they are about is somewhere else. This plugin puts each diagnostic on that code:

  • An underline in the editor at the exact token, with the check name, the message, Error Prone's suggested fix and a link to the check's documentation in the tooltip
  • An "Error Prone" tab in the Problems tool window listing every diagnostic in the project
  • Code | Inspect Code and the inspection profile, through the paired Error Prone inspection
  • Build | Run Error Prone, which recompiles every Java source set in full so every file is analysed again

Your build stays the source of truth. The plugin runs no checks of its own and changes nothing about how Error Prone is configured: it reads the diagnostics Gradle reports while the IDE builds. They update with every build — a warning you fixed disappears when the next build compiles that file — and follow your edits in between.

Structured, not scraped. Diagnostics come from Gradle's Problems API through the Tooling API, with their file, line and column, not from parsing console output.

Requires Gradle 8.14 or newer with Error Prone set up in the build (for example with the net.ltgt.errorprone Gradle plugin), and builds run from the IDE. Known limitations are documented in the README.

Not affiliated with Google or the Error Prone project.
